checks: Rational evaluations at all tetrahedral vertices give coordinate unit vectors and the four forms sum to one. On the endpoint heights of each sampled interval exactly one form is negative; its index is 3,2,1,0 at the stated sites. The other forms are strictly positive.
The complete binary-square projection gives exactly four integer intervals. Each is wholly and strictly owned by one cap, so each closed cap has mass one from total four and is necessary.
The four base vertices are extreme in the projected square, hence their tetrahedral complementary fibers are the singleton heights −1,2,2,−1.

The lower endpoint hits −1 at s=1+1/c when c>0 and avoids it for all s when c≤0. The upper endpoint similarly hits 2 when c<1 and avoids it when c≥1. An affine map has equal sums over the diagonals, contradictory to the bounds.
Source 7e247486f83d7d21 §6 contains the exact tetrahedron and the arbitrary exterior-center obstruction.

overlap.comparison: Its chosen complement avoids the whole mixed lattice and hence has no complementary integer points. The present fixed cover has one complementary point at each integer base, creating constraints absent in that theorem.

readability: The four displayed affine forms fix the orientation of both the open cover and its closed cap masses.
review_method: Independent frozen proof read, source and predecessor comparison, and exact rational replay where numerical claims occur.
summary: The complementary tetrahedron gives an exact minimal strict quarter-budget cover with incompatible affine center inequalities.
